question: Ankita sold her watch at 5% loss. If she had sold it for Rs. 300 more, she would have gained 5%. Find the selling price of the watch.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 5% profit − (−5% loss) = 10%

Difference in selling price = Rs. 300

So, 10% of Cost Price = Rs. 300 ⇒ 1% = Rs. 30

Original Selling Price = 95% of Cost Price

Original Selling Price = 95 × 30 = Rs. 2,850

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,850.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loss percentage in the first case = 5%

Profit percentage in the second case = 5%

Difference in selling price = Rs. 300

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price at loss = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100

Selling Price at profit = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

 

 Total Difference = Rs. 300 (10%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the watch be 100x.

⇒ Original Selling Price (SP₁) = 100x − 5% of 100x = 95x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 100x + 5% of 100x = 105x

⇒ Difference in Selling Price = SP₂ − SP₁

⇒ 105x − 95x = 300

⇒ 10x = 300

⇒ x = 30

⇒ Original Selling Price = 95x = 95 × 30 = Rs. 2,850

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2,850.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP)

Cost Price is the amount paid to purchase an article. Selling Price is the price at which the article is sold. Profit or loss is always calculated on the Cost Price unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price on the label of an article. Discount is always offered on the Marked Price. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective net discount is given by the formula (a + b − ab/100)%.
